elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Revised 21.1: "each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000" — bilateral by its terms; no residual language making Customer uncapped.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 21.1 as rendered uses the exact preferred formula: greater of "Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" and "USD 1,000,000" (previously one month of Fees actually paid). Defined "Fees" (cl. 1.5) is the subscription/professional/usage fees payable by Customer, so the basis is fees, not a narrow set-up charge, and the USD 1m floor operates independently.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.2 retained unchanged: "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill" — already mutual and left intact.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Deletion of "without exception" and insertion of "Except for Excluded Claims" in 21.1 lifts the 21.3 categories out of the cap; 21.3 includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims covers "data-protection, or security obligations", now carved out of the 21.1 cap by the new "Except for Excluded Claims" opener.
21.3 lists "its indemnification obligations" as an Excluded Claim; 21.1 no longer says "without exception" and expressly excepts Excluded Claims.
"gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" in 21.3 Excluded Claims, now outside the re-based 21.1 cap.
Same 21.3 Excluded Claims sentence; 21.1 exception restored.
"gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" in 21.3, excepted from 21.1.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 includes "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property", now outside the cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 21.3 as amended: "Customer's obligations to pay undisputed amounts due under this Agreement are not damages and are not limited by this Section." The narrow trigger the deterministic check reacted to (original "undisputed Fees for conforming Services", with cl. 1.5 "Fees" excluding taxes, expenses, interest and implementation charges) has been replaced with all amounts due under the Agreement; the surviving "undisputed" qualifier is a retained Customer-favourable limit, not a narrowing of the category of payment obligations.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 21.1 re-based from one month to "Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim", with a USD 1,000,000 floor.
21.3 Excluded Claims include indemnification obligations; 21.1 now opens "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Confidentiality breach is an Excluded Claim under 21.3, excepted from the 21.1 cap.
Gross negligence listed in 21.3 Excluded Claims, outside the cap.
Wilful misconduct listed in 21.3 Excluded Claims, outside the cap.

reasons: Deviation call is correct: the original 21.1 capped both Parties at one month of Fees "actually paid" and "without exception", which is below the 6-month walk-away floor and pulled indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside an illusory cap notwithstanding 21.3.

All eleven preferred elements are met in operative language: mutual cap, greater-of 12 months' Fees paid or payable measured to the claim plus USD 1,000,000, untouched mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages in 21.2, the full 21.3 Excluded Claims set now genuinely uncapped, and a payment carve-out covering Customer's payment obligations generally.

The deterministic 'preferred payment carve-out covers Customer payment obligations' failure does not survive substantive inspection: the amended 21.3 reaches "undisputed amounts due under this Agreement" rather than the narrow defined-"Fees"-for-conforming-Services subset, and the retained "undisputed" qualifier is an existing Customer-favourable limit that the drafter correctly preserved.

Minimal: only the cap basis, the "without exception" override (replaced by the necessary "Except for Excluded Claims" hook, since 21.3 alone does not lift the categories out of 21.1) and the payment carve-out scope were changed; 21.2 and the Excluded Claims list are untouched, no survival tails, procedures or extra damages categories were added, and the grammatical concord edit in 21.3 is consequential only.

Preserves intent: "Excluded Claims" remains defined in 21.3, "Fees" remains the cl. 1.5 defined term, the direct-damages sentence in 21.2 and the disputed-amounts protection survive without contradiction, and no dangling cross-reference or undefined trigger is created.
